summary: Duplicate downstream job executions after Go SDK streaming retry following partial disconnect
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when using the Go SDK streaming 'function call' path with an external transactional webhook, occasional partial network disconnects cause the SDK to reconnect and retry the call. The external webhook ends up receiving two nearly-identical 'start-job' requests and spins up duplicate downstream jobs (customer CI tasks).

Impact:
- Multiple paid downstream job runs for a single logical user request; customer is seeing doubled infra costs on specific traces.
- Customer-facing workflows occasionally report duplicate artifacts from CI runs.
- Reproducible under moderate packet loss between the customer network and our us-east serving fleet.

Environment:
- Customer: Nimbuslytics (Dedicated)
- SDK: go-sdk v1.8.3 (observed); also reproduced briefly on v1.9.0-rc
- API: hosted Redwood inference (prod, us-east)
- Model: rw-instruct-large-v1 (toolcall used to trigger webhook)
- Observed timeframe: 2026-03-09 18:00 - 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (as provided and extended by support):
1) Customer issues a streaming chat request that includes a function/tool call to trigger their external CI endpoint (POST to /webhook/job/start).
2) During streaming, transient packet loss (simulated with tc/netem) causes the TCP connection to split; the Go SDK reconnects and restarts the stream, sending the same higher-level function call payload again.
3) Redwood ACKs the first call server-side and forwards to customer's webhook; the SDK does not receive the final confirmation because of the disconnect and initiates a retry; the server accepts the second attempt and forwards a duplicate POST to customer's endpoint.
4) Customer webhook creates a job per POST (no de-duplication) resulting in duplicate job runs.

Logs / traces / evidence:
- Trace IDs: 8f3b1a2c-7a9e-4b6f-9f12-3a7a9c2b0001, 8f3b1a2c-7a9e-4b6f-9f12-3a7a9c2b0002 (same parent id, different stream sessions)
- Server access logs show two accepted POST-forwards for the same call id within ~3s.
- Customer provided webhook logs show two separate job-create requests ~3s apart with identical payload body and no idempotency key.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: SDK reconnect behavior may resend top-level function call payload when streaming resumes without observing server-side ack. Confirmed by reproducer using netem packet drops. Server currently lacks robust de-dup for incoming forwarded webhook requests unless explicit idempotency tokens are present. Observed behavior across go-sdk v1.8.3 and v1.9.0-rc; JS/TS SDKs behave differently (they attach a per-call nonce by default), which explains fewer reports from JS customers.

Key technical findings:
- The Go SDK re-emits the same function-call envelope on reconnect if it hasn't received the final terminal event.
- Server accepts both envelopes as separate invocations because payloads are identical but no call-level idempotency header existed.
- Duplicate forward contains identical call_id value in payload, but server-side matching currently uses a combination of session id + envelope sequence which differs across reconnects; therefore matching fails.
- Patch options considered:
  1) SDK: auto-add Idempotency-Key header per call (simple, immediate customer-facing fix).
  2) Server: widen de-dup matching to include logical call_id inside envelope across sessions (requires careful windowing to avoid memory growth).
  3) Docs: explicit best-practices (recommend customer include idempotency_key).
resolution_notes:
Short-term (customer facing): Advised Nimbuslytics to add an application-level 'Idempotency-Key' header to their webhook which they implemented; their downstream job system deduped on that key and no further duplicates observed in follow-up runs.

Medium-term (platform): Engineering merged go-sdk PR to add an optional per-call 'X-Redwood-Call-Id' header when a function/tool call is serialized; server change to consult the envelope-level call id across reconnects has a PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/978) and is scheduled for canary on 2026-03-16.

Customer communication: Notified customer of workaround and ETA for server fix. Offered to review their webhook idempotency handling and included example Go/TS snippets.

Follow-up items: see next_steps.
next_steps:
- 2026-03-16: Monitor canary rollout of server de-dup patch in us-east; verify traces show only one forward per logical call.
- Update Go SDK release notes and ship v1.9.1 with optional X-Redwood-Call-Id enabled by default.
- Create KB article in Support: 'Preventing duplicate webhook-triggered side effects' with examples in Go/TS/Python.
- Add an observability alert to detect >1 forward per call_id within 10s window and auto-tag tickets for investigation.
resolution: Mitigated (workaround applied) — awaiting server-side rollout for permanent fix.
